posts.body: MPL means Monitor Position Log for the hall acoustics crew. That log records speaker angles and distances from the stage edge.
The librarian uses MPL to mean Music Part Library, the collection of individual orchestral parts. That collection keeps MPL on its checkout forms.

posts.body: The Frequency Response Sheet, shortened to FRS by the repair bench, records measured output across the test tones.

syntax.body: The Frequency Response Sheet, shortened to FRS by the repair bench, records measured output across the test tones.

posts.body: For the choir office FRS is short for Final Rehearsal Schedule, which sets call times and room bookings; the office still uses FRS on notices.
The shared drive has two uses of FRS. Can the abbreviation alone identify one document?
Network component glossary: CSB means Connection State Buffer, the memory area that retains partially received frames.

syntax.body: Network component glossary: CSB means Connection State Buffer, the memory area that retains partially received frames.

posts.body: Storage component glossary: CSB means Cold Storage Broker, the service that queues retrievals from offline media. Both glossary entries remain current.
The bare label CSB appears in both components, so an unqualified cross-component label does not identify just one component.
Team performance sheet: MLR stands for Match Load Register, the record of playing time and reported exertion for each athlete.
Equipment sheet: MLR stands for Mast Line Replacement, the maintenance operation for a training sailboat. Both uses are approved in their own sheets.
